# 📘 Crunch Engine v3.0.2 — Developer Usage Guide

This document explains how to use Crunch Engine as a rendering library inside your own C++ application.

---

# 🧠 1. Basic Philosophy

Crunch is a **low-level rendering wrapper over OpenGL**.

You are responsible for:

* program structure (`main()`, loop, timing)
* asset loading strategy
* scene logic

Crunch provides:

* window/context setup
* shader compilation helpers
* mesh GPU upload system
* rendering pipeline
* camera transforms

---

# 🚀 2. Minimal Startup Flow

Every Crunch application follows this order:

### ✔ Step 1: Create Window

### ✔ Step 2: Initialize Renderer

### ✔ Step 3: Load + Compile Shaders

### ✔ Step 4: Create Meshes

### ✔ Step 5: Create Camera

### ✔ Step 6: Render Loop

---

# 🪟 3. Window System

### Create a window

```cpp
Crunch::Window window;

if (!window.init())
    return -1;

window.create(800, 600, "My Crunch App");
```

---

### Responsibilities

* Initializes GLFW
* Creates OpenGL 3.3 core context
* Handles buffer swapping
* Processes events

---

### Game loop requirements

You must call:

```cpp
window.windowShouldClose();
window.clear(color);
window.update();
```

every frame.

---

# 🎨 4. Shader System

Crunch separates shader usage into:

## Load shader source

```cpp
Crunch::Shader loader;

const char* vertexSrc = loader.load("assets/vertex.glsl");
const char* fragmentSrc = loader.load("assets/fragment.glsl");
```

---

## Compile shaders

```cpp
uint32_t vs = loader.createShader(GL_VERTEX_SHADER, vertexSrc);
uint32_t fs = loader.createShader(GL_FRAGMENT_SHADER, fragmentSrc);
```

---

### Notes

* Returns raw OpenGL shader IDs
* You are responsible for ensuring files exist
* Compilation errors are reported via OpenGL logs

---

# 🧱 5. Mesh System

Meshes store:

* vertex positions
* indices (optional but recommended)
* GPU buffers (VAO/VBO/EBO internally)

---

## Vertex format

```cpp
struct Crunch::Vertex {
    glm::vec3 position;
};
```

---

## Creating a mesh

```cpp
Crunch::Mesh mesh;

std::vector<Crunch::Vertex> vertices;
std::vector<uint32_t> indices;

mesh.create(vertices, indices);
```

---

## Example: Quad

```cpp
vertices = {
    {{ 0.5f,  0.5f, 0.0f }},
    {{ 0.5f, -0.5f, 0.0f }},
    {{-0.5f, -0.5f, 0.0f }},
    {{-0.5f,  0.5f, 0.0f }}
};

indices = {
    0, 1, 3,
    1, 2, 3
};
```

---

# 🖼️ 6. Renderer3D

The renderer handles:

* shader program binding
* mesh drawing
* camera usage

---

## Initialization

```cpp
Crunch::Renderer3D renderer;
renderer.init(vertexShader, fragmentShader);
```

---

## Drawing

```cpp
renderer.draw(&mesh, &camera);
```

---

### What happens internally

Each draw call:

1. binds shader program
2. binds mesh VAO
3. applies camera transforms
4. issues OpenGL draw call

---

# 🎥 7. Camera System

Crunch currently supports:

```cpp
CRUNCH_CAMERA_TYPE_PERSPECTIVE
CRUNCH_CAMERA_TYPE_ORTHOGRAPHIC
```

---

## Initialization

```cpp
Crunch::Camera camera;
camera.init(CRUNCH_CAMERA_TYPE_PERSPECTIVE);
```

---

## Role of the camera

The camera provides:

* view matrix
* projection matrix
* perspective/orthographic setup

It is passed directly into rendering calls.

---

# 🔁 8. Full Render Loop Example

```cpp
while (!window.windowShouldClose()) {

    window.clear(glm::vec4(0.2f, 0.3f, 0.3f, 1.0f));

    renderer.draw(&mesh, &camera);

    window.update();
}
```

---

# 🧠 9. Data Ownership Model

Crunch does NOT own your objects.

| Object        | Owner |
| ------------- | ----- |
| Window        | User  |
| Renderer      | User  |
| Mesh          | User  |
| Camera        | User  |
| Shader source | User  |

Crunch only manages GPU-side resources internally.

---

# ⚙️ 10. Expected Application Structure

```text
App
 ├── Window (GLFW context)
 ├── Shader loader
 ├── Renderer3D
 ├── Meshes
 ├── Camera
 └── main loop
```

---

# ⚠️ 11. Rules / Constraints

* OpenGL context must exist before renderer init
* Shader must compile before renderer use
* Mesh must be created before drawing
* Camera must be initialized before render calls
* No automatic memory/resource cleanup (v3.0.2)

---

# 🧪 12. Full Minimal Example

```cpp
Crunch::Window window;
if (!window.init()) return -1;
window.create(800, 600, "Crunch App");

Crunch::Shader loader;

const char* vsSrc = loader.load("assets/vertex.glsl");
const char* fsSrc = loader.load("assets/fragment.glsl");

uint32_t vs = loader.createShader(GL_VERTEX_SHADER, vsSrc);
uint32_t fs = loader.createShader(GL_FRAGMENT_SHADER, fsSrc);

Crunch::Renderer3D renderer;
renderer.init(vs, fs);

Crunch::Camera camera;
camera.init(CRUNCH_CAMERA_TYPE_PERSPECTIVE);

Crunch::Mesh mesh;

// define vertices + indices...

mesh.create(vertices, indices);

while (!window.windowShouldClose()) {
    window.clear(glm::vec4(0.2f, 0.3f, 0.3f, 1.0f));

    renderer.draw(&mesh, &camera);

    window.update();
}
```

---

# 🔮 13. Version 3.0.2 Limitations

* No texture system yet
* No transform hierarchy
* No scene graph
* No input abstraction
* No physics integration

---

# 🧠 Final Summary

Crunch Engine v3.0.2 gives you:

> A deterministic OpenGL rendering pipeline with explicit control and minimal boilerplate.

You are responsible for structure. Crunch is responsible for graphics.
